messages.subject: Follow-up | Strategic Value Creation Brief for Aker Solutions
messages.body:
Dear Mr. Ørbeck,

Following my earlier introduction to Aker Solutions, I prepared a concise strategic value brief focused on the company's current execution priorities and the areas where my background may add value.

The paper addresses institutional alignment around major energy projects, carbon capture and removal stakeholder readiness, local-value delivery and cross-market executive risk governance. My experience across government relations, ESG, corporate affairs, social performance and regulated project coordination is directly relevant to these interfaces.

My executive CV is included in the final three pages. I would welcome a confidential discussion regarding international leadership needs across government relations, stakeholder strategy, strategic partnerships, sustainability or country-facing execution.

Kind regards,
Ragunauth Ramsaroop
Liaison Director, Social Responsibility Department | AGM Inc.
ragunauthramsaroop@icloud.com
ragunauthramsaroop.com
linkedin.com/in/ragunauth-ramsaroop

strategic_brief.title: Strategic Value Creation Brief for Aker Solutions
strategic_brief.executive_summary: Aker Solutions combines a large project backlog, deep engineering capability and growing exposure to lower-carbon energy systems at a time of leadership transition and tighter scrutiny of capital discipline. Its portfolio increasingly links conventional energy, carbon capture, carbon removal, digital delivery and complex infrastructure execution. These activities depend on credible government engagement, regulatory coordination, local participation and stakeholder confidence alongside technical performance. My director-level experience across government relations, ESG, corporate affairs, social performance and cross-functional project coordination would support Aker Solutions by strengthening institutional alignment and converting external commitments into clear, measurable execution across priority markets.
strategic_brief.company_context: Aker Solutions reported second-quarter 2026 revenue of NOK 13.1 billion and a backlog of NOK 77.2 billion, providing significant forward visibility across a broad energy project portfolio. In August 2026, the company announced a collaboration with Microsoft to accelerate carbon capture and carbon dioxide removal projects, creating a stronger commercial and stakeholder interface around climate infrastructure. In September 2026, Paal Eikeseth was appointed Chief Executive Officer, adding a new leadership chapter while the company continues to balance project execution, capital discipline and growth. Across these priorities, project success depends on more than engineering scope. National policy, permitting, industrial strategy, local participation, environmental commitments, client confidence and public-sector relationships influence timing, economics and reputation across multiple jurisdictions.

opportunities.title: Carbon capture stakeholder bankability
opportunities.rationale: Carbon capture and removal projects require alignment across emitters, governments, regulators, infrastructure providers, technology partners and capital providers. Commercial progress depends on policy certainty, permitting, credible environmental evidence and clear allocation of responsibilities across the project ecosystem.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would structure stakeholder maps, commitment registers and executive issue tracking around priority carbon projects, linking policy dependencies, environmental evidence, government engagement and commercial ownership so external risks are visible before they affect investment or delivery decisions.

opportunities.title: Major project institutional alignment
opportunities.rationale: Aker Solutions operates on complex projects where national energy policy, permitting, procurement expectations and state-linked clients can influence scope and schedule. A consistent institutional approach can improve coordination across markets while preserving the local knowledge needed for effective execution.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would build country-level engagement plans connecting ministries, regulators, clients, local authorities and internal project owners, supported by escalation protocols and evidence-based reporting that links external dependencies directly to project milestones and executive decisions.

opportunities.title: Local value and stakeholder delivery
opportunities.rationale: Local supplier participation, workforce development and community expectations increasingly affect competitiveness on large energy projects. Strong governance helps translate commitments into measurable outcomes and gives clients and public institutions greater confidence in delivery beyond the technical contract scope.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would establish measurable local-value and stakeholder action plans with named owners across procurement, HR, project management, sustainability and external affairs, drawing on operating experience coordinating public institutions, contractors, communities and internal functions in a regulated resource environment.

opportunities.title: Cross-market executive risk governance
opportunities.rationale: A large backlog across multiple technologies and jurisdictions creates external risks that can be fragmented across individual projects. A common governance model for regulatory, social, environmental and institutional issues improves executive visibility and supports earlier intervention when risks begin to affect delivery.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would create a concise executive dashboard covering country risk, permits, stakeholder commitments, community issues and institutional dependencies, with clear thresholds for escalation and periodic cross-functional review across project, legal, commercial, sustainability and leadership teams.

days_0_30: Map priority projects, institutions, regulatory dependencies and external commitments.
Review current ownership of stakeholder, local-value and environmental actions.
Identify external risks with direct schedule, capital or reputation impact.
days_31_60: Align project, government, sustainability, commercial and local-value engagement plans.
Create a single issue and commitment register with named owners and deadlines.
Define executive indicators for institutional alignment and stakeholder delivery.
days_61_90: Run focused engagement on the highest-priority regulatory and institutional dependencies.
Embed monthly cross-functional review of external risks and commitments.
Strengthen evidence controls for local-value and environmental claims.
days_91_180: Scale the governance model across priority projects and markets.
Measure issue closure, stakeholder response times and commitment performance.
Codify lessons into a repeatable project and country stakeholder playbook.

potential_impact: Earlier visibility and resolution of regulatory, institutional and stakeholder risks.
Stronger bankability support for carbon capture and removal projects through clearer external alignment.
More consistent local-value and environmental commitment delivery across major projects.
Improved executive oversight of cross-market risks tied to schedule, capital and reputation.
background_relevance: Director-level leadership across government relations, ESG, corporate affairs, social performance and executive advisory in a multinational resource business.
Direct experience coordinating ministries, regulators, communities, contractors and internal project teams around permits and strategic commitments.
Cross-functional execution across operations, legal, finance, procurement, environment, HR and executive leadership.
Practical experience with carbon-data traceability, renewable-energy positioning and environmental-management systems.
